findings.trigger_condition: An edge stream contains nodes that compare equal under == (such as set({1}) and frozenset({1})), where one node is hashable and the other is unhashable.
findings.root_cause: _id_of segregates node registration into two isolated lookup tables: hashable nodes query hash_buckets while unhashable nodes raise TypeError and query unhashable_nodes. When registering a hashable node, _id_of never checks unhashable_nodes; when registering an unhashable node, the except block never checks hash_buckets or nodes_by_id for equal hashable candidates.
findings.impact: Nodes comparing equal across the hashability boundary are assigned distinct node IDs. This causes duplicate nodes in output layers, corrupted topological ordering, and failure to detect directed cycles (e.g. dependency_layers([(set({1}), frozenset({1}))]) returns a 2-layer result instead of raising DependencyCycleError).
findings.suggested_validation: Execute dependency_layers([(set({1, 2}), frozenset({1, 2}))]). Since set({1, 2}) == frozenset({1, 2}), this represents a directed self-cycle and should raise DependencyCycleError, but candidate-A returns [[frozenset({1, 2})], [{1, 2}]].

findings.trigger_condition: Input graph contains N unhashable nodes (e.g. dicts or lists).
findings.root_cause: Unhashable node lookup performs a linear scan over unhashable_nodes using zip(unhashable_ids, unhashable_nodes) for every unhashable node encountered.
findings.impact: Node ID resolution degrades to O(N) per unhashable node, causing overall O(N^2) time complexity for processing graphs with N unhashable nodes.
findings.suggested_validation: Run dependency_layers on an edge list with 10,000 unique list nodes (e.g. [([i], [i+1]) for i in range(10000)]) and observe quadratic execution time scaling compared to hashable node inputs.
